about: Our Orthopaedics department offers comprehensive musculoskeletal care — from fracture management and sports injuries to total knee and hip replacement. Led by Dr. Shahrukh Khan, we combine clinical expertise with modern surgical techniques to restore mobility and quality of life.

faqs.q: When is knee replacement recommended?
faqs.a: Knee replacement is advised when severe arthritis causes pain that limits daily activities and conservative treatments (physiotherapy, injections) no longer help.

faqs.q: Is arthroscopy a major surgery?
faqs.a: No. Arthroscopy is minimally invasive — 2-3 small incisions, same-day or overnight stay, faster recovery than open surgery.

faqs.q: Can sports injuries heal without surgery?
faqs.a: Many sports injuries (mild sprains, muscle strains) heal with RICE, physiotherapy and PRP. Ligament tears like ACL often need surgical reconstruction for full return to sport.

faqs.q: How long is recovery after hip replacement?
faqs.a: Most patients walk the next day and resume daily activities in 4–6 weeks. Full recovery takes 3–6 months.

homeBlurb: Brain, spine & endovascular neurosurgery. Minimally invasive procedures by AIIMS-trained surgeons.
about: Led by Dr. Simranjeet Singh — an M.Ch from AIIMS with fellowship training in endovascular neurosurgery — our Neurosurgery department handles complex brain tumours, spinal disorders, stroke interventions and vascular malformations. We offer both open and minimally invasive endovascular approaches.
consultantLine: Dr. Simranjeet Singh (MBBS MAMC, M.Ch Neurosurgery AIIMS, Fellowship Endovascular)

faqs.q: What is endovascular neurosurgery?
faqs.a: Endovascular neurosurgery treats blood vessel problems in the brain (aneurysms, AVMs) through a thin catheter via the groin — no open brain surgery needed, faster recovery.

faqs.q: Can a slipped disc heal without surgery?
faqs.a: Yes, 90% of disc problems improve with physiotherapy, pain management and time. Surgery is reserved for persistent neurological weakness or failed conservative care.

faqs.q: What are early warning signs of a brain tumour?
faqs.a: New or worsening headaches (especially morning), seizures, vision/speech changes, memory issues, or unexplained personality changes warrant urgent MRI evaluation.

faqs.q: How soon after a stroke should I seek help?
faqs.a: Immediately — call an ambulance. Clot-busting medication works within 4.5 hours and mechanical thrombectomy within 24 hours of onset. Time = brain cells.

about: Led by Dr. Rupali Raj — trained at Lady Hardinge Medical College and GTB Hospital, with further fellowship in minimally invasive surgery — our Gynaecology & Obstetrics department offers expert consultations in pregnancy care, gynaecological surgery, fertility evaluation, and reproductive health for women of all ages, including high-risk obstetrics.
consultantLine: Dr. Rupali Raj (MBBS Lady Hardinge, MS Obs & Gynae GTB Hospital, FMAS)

faqs.q: When should I see a gynaecologist?
faqs.a: Any time you notice irregular periods, pelvic pain, unusual discharge, or are planning a pregnancy — plus annual preventive check-ups from age 21, including cervical and breast cancer screening.

faqs.q: Is laparoscopic surgery safe?
faqs.a: Yes. Laparoscopic (keyhole) surgery uses small incisions, causes less pain and blood loss, and allows faster recovery than open surgery for most gynaecological conditions, including fibroids and ovarian cysts.

faqs.q: How is a high-risk pregnancy monitored?
faqs.a: High-risk pregnancies (with conditions like gestational diabetes, hypertension, or a history of complications) are monitored with more frequent visits, additional scans, and close blood pressure and growth tracking to ensure a safe delivery.

faqs.q: How is PCOS managed?
faqs.a: PCOS is managed with a combination of lifestyle changes, weight management, and medication to regulate periods, manage symptoms, and support fertility when planning a pregnancy.

name: Paediatrics & Child Health
tagline: Compassionate child healthcare from newborn to adolescent
homeBlurb: Newborn to adolescent care — vaccinations, growth monitoring, illness management & nutrition.
about: Our Paediatrics department provides comprehensive healthcare for children from birth through adolescence. Services include routine well-child visits, immunisation, developmental assessments, management of acute illnesses (fever, diarrhoea, infections) and chronic conditions (asthma, anaemia, ADHD).

faqs.q: When should I take my child to the doctor for fever?
faqs.a: Infants <3 months with any fever, or children with fever >103°F (39.4°C), fever lasting >3 days, rash, difficulty breathing, or persistent vomiting — visit immediately.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 vaccination schedule different?
faqs.a: Yes, India updated NIS 2026 — it now includes rotavirus booster, pneumococcal vaccines and HPV for girls aged 9-14. Ask our paediatrician for a personalised catch-up schedule.

faqs.q: How do I know if my child has ADHD?
faqs.a: Signs include persistent inattention, hyperactivity or impulsivity beyond what is typical for the child's age, present in at least two settings (home + school) and affecting functioning for 6+ months.

faqs.q: What should I do if my baby has jaundice?
faqs.a: Mild jaundice in the first week is common. Severe yellowing, yellow in whites of eyes, poor feeding or sleepiness needs phototherapy — visit us promptly.

faqs.q: Do I need a doctor's referral for an X-ray?

faqs.q: How soon will I get my ultrasound report?

faqs.q: Do you offer Colour Doppler?
